topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: Answer the following about the namesakes of airports around the world.
question.text: This former New York City mayor is the namesake of an airport which Joe Biden compared to a "third world country".
question.answerHtml: Fiorello La Guardia [or Fiorello Henry La Guardia or Fiorello Enrico La Guardia]
question.clue: While in Congress, this man worked with George Norris to co-sponsor an act that banned yellow-dog contracts.

swap.leadin: This is the common name for the Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance program.
swap.text: What federal program provides income to millions of retired people?
swap.clue: The Supreme Court case Flemming v. Nestor established that Congress can revise and amend this policy, which was expanded to include disability in 1954.

question.text: The Great Depression led to the election of Franklin Roosevelt, whose thrity nightly radio addresses from 1933 to 1934 were given this name due to their intimate and calming nature.
question.clue: Similar speeches were given while their speaker was Governor of New York.

swap.leadin: Give the following about attempts to ease the Great Depression.
swap.text: This 1933 law, named for two Democratic senators, created the FDIC. It also notably forbade commercial banks from many investment activities, a measure repealed in 1999.
swap.answerHtml: Glass-Steagall Act (prompt on "Banking Act of 1933;” accept logical equivalents for Act, including Bill and Law)
swap.clue: Support for it came from a New York City prosecutor named Ferdinand Pecora, and one of its namesakes was a Virginia Senator who later served as Truman's Secretary of the Treasury.

question.text: The Second New Deal featured this bill, which established the rights of workers to form labor unions and engage in collective bargaining. It is alternatively known as the National Labor Relations Act of 1935.
question.clue: It was called unconstitutional by the American Liberty League and, in a Supreme Court case, Jones and Laughlin Steel claimed that it was not consistent with the commerce clause, but Chief Justice Hughes sided with the government.

swap.leadin: This group camped on Anacostia Flats and was led by Walter Waters.
swap.text: Name this group of angry World War I veterans who, in 1932, demanded early payments of their pension.
swap.clue: Pelham Glassford twice reinstated Walter Waters as the leader of this group, which Gladwin Bland described as "an immense hobo jungle."

question.leadin: If Franklin D. Roosevelt had had Twitter, he might often use the hashtag #newdealproblems. Answer some questions about such problems he ran into.
question.text: This autocratic Louisiana Senator, nicknamed "Kingfish," threatened a more radical "Share Our Wealth" program. He was organizing a Presidential run at the time of his 1935 assassination.
question.clue: He joined the Senate in 1932 in name only, not traveling to Washington for years.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the founder of the Fifth Party System.
swap.text: One of the major contributors to the New Deal was this member of the Brain Trust, who was the first director of the New York City Planning Commission and later governed Puerto Rico.
swap.clue: In another role, this man was influenced by the ideas of Clarence Perry and Clarence Stein in trying to design three thousand self-sufficient communities while working with John Lansill, those communities being known as Greenbelt Towns.

question.text: Its namesake act was signed into law by Hoover in June of 1930. It arrived at its rates by adopting Senate rates on farm products and House rates on manufactures. Hurting foreign trade when other countries responded with tariffs of their own, it merely prolonged the Great Depression. For 15 points-name this tarriff, the highest in American history.
question.answerHtml: Smoot-Hawley tariff [or Hawley-Smoot tariff; or Tariff Act of 1930; prompt on Tariff Act]
question.clue: Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 as a direct Democratic response to this Republican legislation.

swap.text: The Communist Party tried to bribe Victoria Price to change her testimony against this group, defended by Samuel Leibowitz. For 15 points, Powell v. Alabama overturned some convictions of what group of nine black youths falsely charged with rape?
swap.clue: James Horton presided over a trial of this group for the "god fearing people of Decatur County;" in that trial, Samuel Leibowitz defended them for the American Communist Party.

question.text: In the meta-novel The Grasshopper Lies Heavy, Roosevelt survives the assassination attempt and Rexford Tugwell, a member of this group of Roosevelt advisors, many of whom were Columbia University professors, becomes president.
question.clue: Rexford Tugwell was a member of this group, another of whom developed the term "Forgotten Man" that was often used in speeches.

swap.text: David Lilienthal headed this New Deal agency through its efforts to modernize its namesake agrarian region via the production of about 30 dams in the eastern United States.
swap.clue: A seven-rule test to apply constitutional avoidance was developed to rule in favor of this agency in the Ashwander case.

question.leadin: Identify the following female senators from American history.
question.text: The widow of an Arkansan senator shocked her colleagues after using an invitation to stand in for Vice President Charles Curtis to announce she would seek new election in 1932. She won, becoming the first woman elected for a full term.
question.clue: This female Senator from Arkansas who served until 1944 when she was replaced by J. William Fulbright.

swap.text: The Child Labor Amendment, passed shortly after Hammer v. Dagenhart, was superseded by this 1938 act, which prohibited people under 18 from working under conditions of "oppressive child labor."
swap.clue: This 1938 law outlawed "oppressive child labor" and established the first minimum wage at twenty-five cents an hour.

question.leadin: This man got his start working at his brother James's tavern in the West Bottoms area.
question.text: Name this political boss who controlled Jackson County in the early 20th century. His downfall came after Lloyd Stark investigated him for income tax evasion.
question.clue: This political boss who built his machine from Kansas City, Missouri and brought people such as Guy Brasfield Park to power.

swap.text: As Hennepin County Attorney, Olson filed a public nuisance injunction against the antisemitic Saturday Press, leading to this Supreme Court case that found prior restraint of the newspaper in violation of the First Amendment.
swap.clue: As Chief Justice, Hughes wrote the majority opinion in this 1931 case supporting freedom of the press. This case struck down a Minnesota law targeting "scandalous" newspapers.

question.leadin: John Hart Ely's Democracy and Distrust builds on Justice Harlan Stone's opinion in this case by arguing that the Warren Court's activism was not values-based but process-based.
question.text: Name this Supreme Court case, whose Footnote Four introduced the basis for strict scrutiny by proposing a "narrower scope for operation of the presumption of constitutionality."
question.clue: This 1938 Supreme Court case, which is more famous for its "footnote four."

swap.leadin: TIME named the leader of this agency, Hugh S. Johnson, as its 1933 Man of the Year instead of FDR after he implemented industry codes to ensure "fair competition."
swap.text: A blue eagle and the motto "We Do Our Part" were used to represent what agency, which was dissolved after the Supreme Court ruled its regulations were unconstitutional in the "sick chicken" case?
swap.clue: General Hugh Johnson was made the director of this agency, which was created by an act that set up a group of fair competition codes for industry.

question.text: The effectiveness of the RFC was somewhat compromised by the requirement that it publish the names of the banks receiving loans, which was forced by this Speaker of the House and later Vice President. His nickname referred to his endorsement of the cactus as a state flower.
question.clue: For a time, the so-called "Board of Education" was known as his "Dog House" because of his ability to forcibly persuade fellow Congressmen.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a piece of legislation FTPE.
swap.text: This 1933 piece of legislation sought to raise and stabilize farm prices, store reserves, and control production.
swap.clue: In U.S. v. Butler, the Supreme Court ruled that the production control and processing tax elements of this 1933 act, which aimed to eliminate crop surpluses, were unconstitutional.
